chapters.title: Chapter 1: Why These Three Documents Matter

lessons.title: Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS: What Each One Is and Who Issues It

children.text: In the last lesson you saw how employers, banks, registrars and brokers report your income against your PAN. That raw data reaches you in three documents. Most first-time filers treat them as interchangeable. They are not. Each one answers a different question, and each one is issued by someone different.

stats.label: Form 16
stats.context: What was deducted from my salary, and how was it worked out?

stats.label: Form 26AS
stats.context: What TDS and TCS credit do I have?

stats.label: AIS
stats.context: What does the department know about my financial year?

children.text: Form 16: The Salary TDS Certificate
Form 16 is a TDS certificate that your employer must give you for tax deducted from your salary under section 392 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 192 of the 1961 Act). It is due by
15 June
after the end of the financial year. It has two parts, and they come from two different places.
Part A: Generated Through TRACES
Part A is not typed up by your HR team. After the employer files its quarterly TDS statements, it downloads Part A from
TRACES
. It shows the employer's name and
TAN
, your PAN, the period of employment, and the TDS deducted and deposited in each quarter along with the receipt number of each quarterly statement.

markDefs.definition: TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System, the Income Tax Department portal that processes TDS statements and generates TDS certificates.
Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number, the 10-character ID every deductor quotes in its TDS filings.

children.text: Because Part A comes from the department's own records, its TDS figure should always match what Form 26AS shows against that employer.
Part B: Prepared by Your Employer

Part B is the employer's working. It shows your gross salary, exempt allowances such as HRA, the standard deduction, deductions you declared, the tax regime used, and the final tax payable. If you receive perquisites such as a company car or ESOP allotments, the employer also attaches Form 12BA listing their taxable value.
Part B is where mistakes usually hide, because it depends on what you declared to HR and when. We take it apart line by line in Chapter 2.

body.text: No TDS, no Form 16. Form 16 is a certificate of tax deducted, so if your salary was below the taxable limit and your employer deducted nothing, it is not required to issue one. You still have to report your salary correctly. Ask HR for a salary statement instead.

body.title: Form 16 vs Form 16A: which one is which?

children.text: Form 16 covers TDS on salary only. For TDS on other payments, such as interest on an FD, the deductor issues
Form 16A
. Form 16A is issued every quarter, within 15 days of the due date of the quarterly TDS statement, so by 15 August, 15 November, 15 February and 15 June.
You rarely need Form 16A in practice, because every entry it contains also appears in Form 26AS. If a bank has not sent you one, Form 26AS is enough to check the credit.
Form 26AS: Your Tax Credit Statement

Form 26AS is generated by the department, not by any payer. It pulls together every quarterly TDS and TCS statement filed against your PAN by every deductor and collector: your employer, your banks, a buyer of your property, a company paying you dividends. It also shows refunds paid to you and any TDS or TCS defaults recorded during processing.

You open it from the e-filing portal, which redirects you to TRACES. Think of it as the ledger of tax already paid on your behalf. When your return claims TDS credit, that claim is matched against the statements shown here.

body.text: Form 26AS got narrower in 2023. From AY 2023-24 onward it shows only TDS and TCS related data. Advance tax, self-assessment tax and high-value transactions reported through SFT moved to AIS. Older guides that tell you to check advance tax in Form 26AS are out of date.

children.text: AIS: The Annual Information Statement
The Annual Information Statement was launched on 1 November 2021 to give taxpayers the widest possible view of what has been reported against their PAN in a financial year. It has two parts.
Part A: General information.
Your PAN, name, date of birth, contact details and address.
Part B: Everything reported.

It is split into TDS and TCS information, SFT information such as interest, dividends and securities sales, payment of taxes such as advance tax and self-assessment tax, demands and refunds, and other information such as salary details and foreign remittances.
You can download AIS in PDF, JSON or CSV format from the e-filing portal. The CSV is the one to use if you want to sort and total entries in a spreadsheet.
TIS: The Summary Built From AIS
Alongside AIS sits the
Taxpayer Information Summary

. AIS lists every entry separately, for example 12 separate dividend credits. TIS rolls them into one figure per category, such as total dividend income. It shows two columns: the value processed by the system, and the value accepted by you or confirmed by the source after feedback. The accepted values are what pre-fill your return.

markDefs.definition: TIS: a category-wise summary of AIS, showing the value processed by the system and the value after your feedback. The accepted values are used to pre-fill your return.

children.text: If an AIS entry is wrong, for example a sale that is duplicated or interest that belongs to a joint holder, you can submit feedback on it. Chapter 4 walks through how.
All Three Side by Side

cells: Salary and TDS on salary from one employer
All TDS and TCS against your PAN, refunds, defaults
TDS and TCS, SFT data, taxes paid, demands, refunds, other information
From HR or the payroll portal
e-Filing portal, then Annual Information Statement
Ask the employer to correct and reissue
Ask the deductor to file a correction statement

children.text: Priya's Three Documents

Back to Priya from Pune. In FY 2025-26 her employer deducted ₹1,74,000 from her ₹18 lakh salary. She also had two FDs: SBI paid ₹38,000 of interest with no TDS because it was below the ₹50,000 threshold, and ICICI Bank paid ₹62,000 and deducted TDS at 10%, which is ₹6,200. She received ₹6,000 in dividends from HDFC Bank, below the ₹10,000 dividend TDS threshold, and redeemed mutual fund units for ₹2,40,000.

body.text: Form 16 tells you about one employer. Form 26AS tells you about tax already paid for you. AIS tells you what the department thinks you earned. You need all three to file with confidence.

body.label: The order to check them in
body.context: Start narrow with your salary, confirm every tax credit, then look for income you may have forgotten.

children.text: Check Your Understanding

body.title: Priya's total TDS credit
body.prompt: Using Priya's figures above, what total TDS credit should her Form 26AS show for FY 2025-26?
body.explanation: Only amounts where tax was actually deducted appear as credits: ₹1,74,000 from her employer plus ₹6,200 from ICICI Bank = ₹1,80,200. SBI interest, the dividend and the redemption had no TDS, so they appear only in AIS.

body.title: Where did the advance tax go?
body.question: Priya paid ₹15,000 of advance tax in March 2026 for her capital gains. Which document should she check to confirm the payment was recorded against her PAN?
body.explanation: From AY 2023-24, Form 26AS shows only TDS and TCS related data. Advance tax and self-assessment tax appear in AIS under payment of taxes. Form 16 and Form 16A cover only tax deducted by a payer.

body.title: Which part comes from TRACES?
body.textWithBlank: Part ___ of Form 16, showing quarterly TDS deducted and deposited, is generated through TRACES.
body.explanation: Part A is generated through TRACES from the employer's quarterly TDS statements. Part B, the salary and tax working, is prepared by the employer.

body.title: Arjun's missing quarter
body.scenario: Arjun works for a mid-sized firm in Gurugram. His Form 16 Part B says ₹90,000 of TDS was deducted in FY 2025-26, ₹22,500 each quarter. When he opens Form 26AS in late June, it shows only ₹67,500 against his employer's TAN.
body.prompt: What has most likely gone wrong, and what should Arjun do before filing?
body.modelAnswer: ₹67,500 is exactly three quarters of ₹22,500, so one quarterly TDS statement is missing, most likely Q4, which was due on 31 May. Either it was not filed, it was filed with an error in his PAN, or it has not been processed yet. Arjun should check Part A of his Form 16: if Part A also shows only three quarters, his employer has not reported the fourth. He should write to HR asking them to file or correct the statement, then recheck Form 26AS. If he files before it is fixed, his claim for the missing ₹22,500 will not match and he may receive a tax demand.

body.title: Your 10-minute document check
steps: Log in to the e-filing portal with your PAN and confirm your name and date of birth in AIS Part A.
Get Form 16 from HR or your payroll portal for each employer you had during the year.
Open Form 26AS and note the TDS shown against each employer's TAN.
Confirm each employer total matches Part A of the matching Form 16.
Download AIS as CSV and list every interest, dividend and securities sale entry.
Mark anything in AIS you do not recognise for feedback.

body.text: Coming next: from Tax Year 2026-27, Form 16 becomes Form 130, and Form 26AS and AIS are brought together in Form 168 under the Income-tax Act, 2025. The next lesson explains what changes and what stays the same.

body.label: AIS help page, Income Tax Department
body.description: Official guide to viewing AIS and TIS, downloading them and submitting feedback.

points: Form 16 is issued by your employer by 15 June and covers only salary and TDS on salary.
Part A of Form 16 comes from TRACES and should match Form 26AS. Part B is the employer's own working.
If no tax was deducted from your salary, your employer does not have to issue Form 16.
Form 26AS shows only TDS and TCS related data, plus refunds and defaults, from AY 2023-24 onward.
AIS is the widest view: TDS, TCS, SFT data, advance and self-assessment tax, demands and refunds.
TIS summarises AIS by category, and the accepted values pre-fill your return.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects the rules as of September 2026. Thresholds and form formats can change through Budgets and CBDT notifications. For your specific situation, check the e-filing portal or consult a chartered accountant.
